data.text: is this question for the status - what waits on me driven by claude or by the ddflow? if it is not ddflow, should we think of improving the periodical info that ddflow reports to also report progress, status, potential eta and what is waiting on the user, so if the user has missed it to be able to ask, as I periodically do

Operator answers 2026-10-23 to OD proposal Q1-Q9 (relayed by the lead; each equals the proposal default): Q1 option C built as B first; Q2 queue lists only entries a person must answer, lead-owned entries behind --all; Q3 escalate_after = nudge at creation, 'needs' after 1h, 'urgent' after 24h, red main 6h; Q4 fold AW-inbox, DX-status-digest, AW-since-cursor into OD-queue/OD-digest/OD-seen; Q5 ETA in digest and Progress: per phase as labelled range 'estimate', never in SessionStart; Q6 SessionStart/brief one line: count, oldest age, top 3 titles; Q7 push through AW-sinks on new entry, red main, spend limit, plus one daily digest, quiet hours 22:00-07:00 except red main; Q8 relay rule enforced (show entries verbatim, ask with digest --ask); Q9 docs/ddflow/DIGEST.md committed, regenerated by ddflow export on cadence.

data.alternatives: A: extend status (pull only, bloats status). B only: no push so missed items stay missed.
data.consequences: Needs AW-sinks for the C part; B ships first.
data.context: What waits on the operator is compiled by the model; ddflow shows one approvals line.
data.decision: Option C (digest view + brief hook, then sinks and DIGEST.md), delivered as B first; stopping at B is complete for the question asked. Operator 2026-10-23: accepted the default.
data.title: Operator digest: option C, built as B first

data.alternatives: One list for both: noisy, hides what only the operator can answer.
data.consequences: Every entry needs an owner field; --all must exist.
data.context: Lead-owned items would drown the operator's list.
data.decision: The default queue lists only entries a person must answer; lead-owned entries are behind --all.
data.title: Operator queue lists only person-owned entries

data.alternatives: No escalation / fixed severity: a missed item stays quiet.
data.consequences: Severity is a function of now; knobs layered per D-config-layer-order.
data.decision: [digest] escalate_after = nudge at creation, 'needs' after 1h, 'urgent' after 24h; escalate_after_red_main = 6h. Severity rises with age and an entry never disappears by being shown.
data.title: Escalation of unanswered entries

data.alternatives: Keep separate and make OD depend on them: duplicated cursor/inbox logic.
data.consequences: Held items cannot be folded now; they are linked and reconciled on release.
data.context: Three overlapping designs for one need.
data.decision: Fold AW-inbox into OD-queue, DX-status-digest into OD-digest, AW-since-cursor into OD-seen. Run 'ddflow task fold' only for items nobody holds; for held ones link and note.
data.title: Fold AW-inbox, DX-status-digest, AW-since-cursor into OD

data.alternatives: Nowhere (no answer to the operator's ask); everywhere (spam, false precision).
data.consequences: Needs ETA methods with sample-size confidence.
data.context: ETA guesses erode trust and cost tokens at every session start.
data.decision: ETA appears in the digest and in Progress: per phase as a labelled range marked 'estimate' (method named, conditional on pending operator answers, 'unavailable' when data is missing); never in SessionStart.
data.title: ETA placement: digest and Progress per phase, labelled range

data.alternatives: Nothing (rule only): model-dependent. Full list: busts the budget.
data.decision: Session start and brief carry exactly one line: count of waiting entries, oldest age, top 3 titles.
data.title: SessionStart/brief carries one queue line

data.alternatives: On change only: no periodic reminder. Never: the miss problem remains.
data.consequences: Depends on AW-sinks; spam and leak risk handled by classes and quiet hours.
data.context: Pull-only misses what the operator is away from.
data.decision: Push through AW-sinks on a new queue entry, red main, spend limit, plus one daily digest; quiet hours default 22:00-07:00 except red main.
data.title: Push through AW-sinks with quiet hours

data.consequences: Needs a prompt/driver line and a test (OD-prompt, OD-e2e).
data.context: Paraphrase drops the answer command and default.
data.decision: Agents and the lead must show queue entries verbatim and ask the operator with 'ddflow digest --ask' (the exact AskUserQuestion payload), not a paraphrase; enforced, not advisory. An agent printing the digest does not count as the operator having seen it.
data.title: Relay rule is enforced

data.alternatives: Local only: invisible to other machines/operators.
data.context: A reviewable, offline copy of the digest.
data.decision: docs/ddflow/DIGEST.md is generated, committed, and regenerated by 'ddflow export' on cadence, not per push.
data.title: Committed docs/ddflow/DIGEST.md

data.body:
Entry: id, what, why, since, default, answer command, blocks (items transitively, from the item graph), owner, severity escalating with age ([digest].escalate_after). Order: severity, impact, age. Replay test: fold the real log of a week, assert counts sane. Folds AW-inbox (proposed). Conformance: every threshold is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt (D-everything-configurable); no new MCP tool (D-mcp-new-nouns); reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB; deterministic (same state and now, same text); research docs/ddflow/research/operator-digest.md, proposal docs/ddflow/decisions/operator-digest.md.

Folded AW-inbox (ddflow inbox: everything waiting on the operator, in one list): D-OD-Q4: operator accepted the fold 2026-10-23.

One read-only list of what only a person can do or decide: items in the 'questions' state (e.g. DX-waves-status) with the question text, proposed (unaccepted) decisions, chore approvals pending (ddflow chore approve is a person's act), bugs or completions that need an override the hook forbids to agents (fix-Bci-ruff-check..., RM-tool-diet-research, B998bcca9ce style), unavailable-reviewer escalations, contested decisions, gates recorded partial/forced awaiting spot-check (ddflow gate list --refuted), expired credentials or quota pauses. Each row: what, since when, who is waiting on it, the exact command to answer it. CLI + MCP, --json, exit 0 even if non-empty (an inbox is not a failure). Also shown as a line in brief and status ('3 items wait for you'). Conformance: every threshold is a knob settable by file, CLI, MCP and prompt (D-everything-configurable); declare new commands with family and action (D-mcp-tool-families); reuse the shared engines; files under 20 KB; no private addresses or keys in tracked files or in any message sent.

Folded DX-status-digest (`ddflow digest [--since 3h]`: what merged, open bugs by owner, wave and track progress, running agents, load, interrupted items, in one view): D-OD-Q4: operator accepted the fold 2026-10-23.

Evidence 2026-10-16: the operator asked 'what is the status' about 20 times; each answer needed 5-8 separate commands plus ad-hoc scripts (bug list greps, per-state tag counts, git log of merges, ddflow next, uptime). Wanted: one command (CLI, MCP, prompt) printing: merges and completions since T; open bugs grouped by owner and by theme; progress by wave: tag and track (wave:N, track:fix/dx, any label) from the label query engine; running agents with their item and wait state (the lease-wait view); interrupted/expired items; machine load and the parallelism cap; the next ready items and why others are held (cap, conflict, deps). Text and --json; the operator view is the same data. Needs LB-search for label queries but ships without it using the tag filter that exists.

data.claim: Every Site.verb is either named by a Source.sites or by EXEMPT_SITES, checked by a pure function
data.falsifier: unregistered_sites() returns a verb for the current SITES, or does not report an injected one
data.mechanism: unregistered_sites() diffs sites.SITES verbs against the table
data.question: Can the operator-queue source table be tied to approvals/sites.py so a new operator-only verb cannot go unlisted?

evidence.note: brief --item read; D-mcp-new-nouns, D-everything-configurable (no thresholds), r-small-files (8 KB), r-reuse-core (sites.py reused)
services/digest/sources.py + tests/test_digest_sources.py, 7 tests pass, ruff clean

chunk_findings.detail: The `approval` source row leaves `sites=()` even though its own `answer` is `ddflow approvals approve <id> | deny <id>`, the operator-only verb(s) for normal pending approvals in `ddflow/services/approvals/sites.py` (e.g. `approvals.approve`/`approvals.deny`). Because `covered_sites()` only collects `s.sites` plus `EXEMPT_SITES`, those normal-approval verbs are omitted, so `unregistered_sites()` will return them and `test_every_operator_only_verb_is_covered_or_exempt` fails. The most common operator-queue entry is then not mapped to the operator-only site that answers it.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/sources.py:62

chunk_findings.detail: `Source.answer` is documented at line 39 as “The exact command that answers it,” and the module docstring repeats that the row carries “the exact command that answers it,” but several rows are natural-language instructions, not commands. Concrete input: an agent run fails on a rate limit; `by_kind()["agent_failed"].answer` is `"restart the agent; raise the limit"`, which is not an executable `ddflow ...` command, so any consumer that renders the answer slot as the documented exact command will present an invalid command. The same problem occurs for `credential` (`"put the key where the reviewer's doc says (never in chat)"`), `question` (`"answer in chat; the lead records it"`), `export_ack` (`"ddflow export ack ..."`), `decision` (`"ddflow decision show <id>, then accept or supersede"`), `gate_spotcheck` (`"ddflow gate list --refuted, then accept or reopen"`), and `lease` (`"ddflow health (its correcting command)"`).
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/sources.py:208,218,228 (and `export_ack`, `decision`, `gate_spotcheck`, `lease` answer rows)

chunk_findings.detail: `assert cmd[v].split(" ")[1] in s.answer` only checks that the word after `"ddflow"` appears anywhere in the source’s answer, not that the full site command appears. For example, if the `force` site command is `"ddflow approve --force"` and a source covering that site has `answer = "ddflow approve"`, the assertion still passes because `"approve"` is present, even though the required `--force` command is missing. This lets incorrect answer commands into the operator-queue table and contradicts the test’s stated purpose.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_digest_sources.py:47

chunk_findings.detail: The `lease` and `agent_failed` sources both use `"lease expired with no heartbeat"` as a `detected_from` condition. For a lease that expired without a heartbeat but has no run-failure record, an OD-queue built from these rows will emit both a `lease` entry and an `agent_failed` entry for the same underlying lease. `agent_failed.what` ("an agent's run failed (rate or spend limit, crash)") is false for an idle lease, and the operator receives an additional alarm while the lead already owns the lease. The failed-run source should not match a bare lease expiry.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/sources.py:213,224

chunk_findings.detail: The `command` field is documented as the runnable `ddflow ...` command that answers or inspects the source, but several rows contain a literal `...` where the CLI requires actual arguments, so the stored command is not runnable. Concrete input: `by_kind()["export_ack"].command` is `"ddflow export ack ..."`; passing that string to a shell fails because `...` is not a valid argument for `ddflow export ack`. The same pattern occurs for `decide` (`...` after `--id`), `gate_skip` (`--reason ...`), `force_completion` (`--force ...`), `plan` (`--reason ...`), and `question` (`...`). A consumer that renders the documented exact command is therefore shown an invalid command.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/digest/sources.py:42,158 (also 87,98,122,170,248)

chunk_findings.detail: Previous finding 2 still holds despite the `command` field and the new prefix check. `_prefix("ddflow approve --force")` returns only `"ddflow approve"` because line 51 deliberately stops at the first option (`w.startswith("-")`), and line 66 only requires `s.command.startswith("ddflow approve")`. Given a source row covering the `force` site whose `command` is `"ddflow approve"` (missing the required `--force`), this assertion passes even though the exact command is incomplete. The required option/suffix after the verb is never verified.
